title: Aran-style multi-cable cardigan
excerpt: An advanced drop-shoulder cardigan in aran yarn with multiple cable panels across the back and front halves. Combines fpdc crossover cables, diamond panels, and seed-stitch grounds. Graded XS to 3XL.
sourceNotes: Aran-style multi-cable cardigans are an advanced crochet garment project that requires careful panel planning.

glossaryTerms.definition: The arrangement of different cable types across the width of the back and front pieces. Each panel has a fixed stitch count, and the panels are placed in a fixed order and repeated symmetrically. A stitch diagram or layout chart marks the boundaries between panels before casting on.
A background of alternating dc and ch-1 spaces between cable panels. The broken texture of seed stitch recedes visually and provides a clear contrast that helps each cable panel read distinctly.

crochet.gaugeText: 14 dc x 16 rows = 10 x 10 cm in aran on a 5 mm hook.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Graded XS to 3XL. Size M: 104.3 cm bust.

content.text: before casting on. This cardigan uses three panel types across the back: an outer fpdc crossover rope cable (8 sts), a central diamond cable (12 sts), and a
fill (variable). The front halves each carry one rope cable at the outer edge and a diamond at centre. Work all pieces flat, then seam and add a 2-button band down each front edge.
Size M: back 146 sts wide, 81.7 cm body. Sleeve 63.3 cm.
Chain 148. Establish panel layout. Work all panels simultaneously for 81.7 cm. Shape neck.
Chain 75 each. Establish cable panels. Work for body height. Shape neck. Add button band.
Chain 56. Work a single rope cable panel at centre sleeve with seed stitch each side, increasing each end every 4 rows for 63.3 cm.
The diamond cable vest is a good place to start with panel work before moving on to multi-panel designs.

Work front panel the same as back, shaping a shallow neckline over the final 17 rows.
Work each sleeve: cast on 50, increase evenly to 98 over 100 rows.
Sew shoulder seams leaving a 41cm gap for the neckline.
Lay each sleeve flat across the open armhole and sew in place along the straight edge.
Sew side seams and underarm seams in one continuous line.
Pick up 58 stitches around the neckline and work neck trim. Weave in ends and block.
